deep.reconstruction:
The page is titled 'Ideen' (bundle Math. 34). It holds three dated or undated research notes. None contains a worked derivation, so the reconstruction below unpacks the content of each.

(1) Astronomy note, 1813 Apr. 2? (the day is obscured by an ink blot). Gauss proposes measuring star declinations with a good repetition theodolite, a horizontal-angle instrument. The method is to measure the star's azimuth difference from a fixed terrestrial mark at greatest eastern elongation and again at greatest western elongation. The underlying spherical astronomy is my reconstruction.
- In the pole-zenith-star triangle, the star is at greatest digression when the parallactic angle is 90 degrees.
- This happens at hour angle t with cos t = tan(phi)/tan(delta). Such an elongation exists only if delta > phi.
- At that moment the zenith distance satisfies cos z = sin(phi)/sin(delta).
- The azimuth A from north satisfies sin A = cos(delta)/cos(phi).
- The eastern and western elongations lie symmetrically about the meridian. The difference of the two azimuth readings against the terrestrial object is therefore 2A, and the mark's own azimuth cancels out.
- Hence cos(delta) = cos(phi) * sin A.

Why 'near the equator' (my interpretation): read it as an observer near the terrestrial equator, where phi is about 0.
- There every star north of the observer's latitude has elongations.
- The relation reduces to cos(delta) ≈ sin A.
- Its sensitivity to latitude error, d(cos delta)/d(phi) = -sin(phi) sin A, nearly vanishes.
- Since refraction does not alter azimuth, only horizontal angles enter. The repetition principle can then be used to beat down division and reading errors.
- So the method is refraction-free and insensitive to latitude, which is the sense of 'schärfste Bestimmung' (sharpest determination).

(2) Foundations note, 1813 Apr. 27. 'In the theory of parallel lines we are still no further than Euclid was. This is the shameful part (partie honteuse) of mathematics, which sooner or later must take a completely different form.' This is a programmatic statement on the parallel postulate, with no derivation. The preceding folio contains an absolute-geometry style proof (Satz 5: no angle of a triangle equals the supplement of another of its angles), done without the parallel axis.

(3) Number-theory note, undated, presumably also 1813. 'Just as a class of truths of higher arithmetic, restricted to real numbers, stands in intimate connection with the circular functions, so the more general truths of higher arithmetic extended to imaginary quantities will be mirrored in the lemniscatic functions. These ideas open the gate to a most rich field of analysis.'
- Modern reading of the first half: quadratic reciprocity and cyclotomy. The Gauss sum g = sum exp(2*pi*i*k^2/p) satisfies g^2 = (-1)^((p-1)/2) p, and the values of sin and cos at rational multiples of pi generate abelian extensions of Q.
- The analogue: biquadratic reciprocity over Z[i], together with division values of the lemniscatic sine sl.
- sl has complex multiplication by Z[i], for example sl(iz) = i sl(z) and sl((1+i)z) = (1+i) sl(z)/sl'(z).
- Its division values generate abelian extensions of Q(i).
- This is the programme later realized by Eisenstein (1850), who proved biquadratic reciprocity via lemniscatic functions, and by Abel (lemniscate division, 1827-28). It ultimately leads to Kronecker's Jugendtraum and complex multiplication.
errors: No mathematical errors, since no computations appear on the page.
Grammatical slip in note 1: 'würde ... gemacht werden könnte' should read 'gemacht werden könnte' or 'würde ... gemacht werden können'.
Grammatical slip in note 3: 'in der Lemniscatischen Functionen' should be 'in den'.

Physical caveat to note 1: greatest digressions exist only for stars with delta > phi. For an equatorial observer this covers practically all northern stars. Stars essentially on the celestial equator itself have elongations only as phi tends to 0, and the azimuth of near-equatorial stars changes slowly, so precise timing is unnecessary. This is an implicit assumption, not an error.

results.what: Declination from azimuths of the eastern and western greatest elongations measured against a terrestrial mark: cos(delta) = cos(phi) sin(A_elong), nearly latitude-independent for an observer near the equator, refraction-free
results.modern_name: Determination of declination from elongation azimuths (method of elongations / horizontal-angle method)
results.usually_credited_to: Elongation formulas are classical spherical astronomy (18th c.). Their use for azimuth and meridian determination is standard in geodesy; using them for precise declinations is not a standard named method.

results.what: Assessment that the theory of parallels is the 'partie honteuse' of mathematics and must take a wholly different form (1813)
Programme: circular functions are to quadratic reciprocity and cyclotomy over Q as lemniscatic functions are to biquadratic reciprocity and higher arithmetic over Z[i]
results.modern_name: Lemniscatic analogue of cyclotomy; complex multiplication by Z[i]; proof of biquadratic reciprocity via the lemniscate
results.usually_credited_to: Eisenstein (1850 proof of biquadratic reciprocity via lemniscatic functions); Abel (1827-28 lemniscate division); Kronecker (Jugendtraum)

deep.surprise_reason: This 'Ideen' sheet is well known. The 1813 parallels remark and the lemniscate/biquadratic-reciprocity remark are printed in Gauss's Werke and cited in the history of non-Euclidean geometry and of reciprocity laws. Gauss's lemniscate work (1797 onward) and biquadratic research are documented. The astronomical note is routine spherical astronomy.
